42444-the-face-of-the-fields.title: The Face Of The Fields
42444-the-face-of-the-fields.creator: Unknown
42444-the-face-of-the-fields.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The hens were still flapping for safety in a dozen directions, but the gray harrier had gone. A bolt of lightning could not have dropped so unannounced, could not have vanished so completely, could scarcely have killed so quickly. I ran to the pullet, but found her dead. The harrier’s stroke, delivered with fearful velocity, had laid head and neck open as with a keen knife.

arxiv-2305-05894.title: Structured Kalman Filter for Time Scale Generation in Atomic Clock Ensembles Thanks: This work is supported by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) under its ”Research and Development for Expansion of Radio Resources (JPJ000254)” program. Yuyue Yan and Takayuki Ishizaki are with
arxiv-2305-05894.creator: Yuyue Yan, Takahiro Kawaguchi, Yuichiro Yano
arxiv-2305-05894.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yuyue Yan, Takahiro Kawaguchi, Yuichiro Yano. In this article, we present a structured Kalman filter associated with the transformation matrix for observable Kalman canonical decomposition from conventional Kalman filter (CKF) in order to generate a more accurate time scale. The conventional Kalman filter is a special case of the proposed structured Kalman filter which yields the same predicted unobservable or observable states when some conditions are satisfied.

arxiv-2310-16805.title: Two-qubit logic between distant spins in silicon
arxiv-2310-16805.creator: Jurgen Dijkema, Xiao Xue, Patrick Harvey-Collard, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, Sander L. de Snoo, Guoji Zheng, Amir Sammak, Giordano Scappucci, Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
arxiv-2310-16805.description: Abstract Direct interactions between quantum particles naturally fall off with distance. For future-proof qubit architectures, however, it is important to avail of interaction mechanisms on different length scales. In this work, we utilize a superconducting resonator to facilitate a coherent interaction between two semiconductor spin qubits 250 µ ​ m 250\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro m} apart.

arxiv-2510-03434.title: Paris: A Decentralized Trained Open-Weight Diffusion Model
arxiv-2510-03434.creator: Zhiying Jiang, Raihan Seraj, Marcos Villagra, Bidhan Roy * Bagel Labs ⋅ \cdot bagel.com
arxiv-2510-03434.description: Abstract We present Paris , the first publicly released diffusion model pre-trained entirely through decentralized computation. Paris demonstrates that high-quality text-to-image generation can be achieved without centrally coordinated infrastructure. Paris is open for research and commercial use. Paris required implementing our Distributed Diffusion Training framework from scratch.

arxiv-2510-22642.title: Data-driven dimensionally decomposed generalized polynomial chaos expansion for forward uncertainty quantification
arxiv-2510-22642.creator: Hojun Choi, Eunho Heo, Dongjin Lee
arxiv-2510-22642.description: Abstract Dimensionally decomposed generalized polynomial chaos expansion (DD-GPCE) efficiently performs forward uncertainty quantification (UQ) in complex engineering systems with high-dimensional random inputs of arbitrary distributions. However, constructing the measure-consistent orthonormal polynomial bases in DD-GPCE requires prior knowledge of input distributions, which is often unavailable in practice.

arxiv-2512-06440.title: Neural expressiveness for beyond importance model compression
arxiv-2512-06440.creator: Angelos-Christos Maroudis, Sotirios Xydis
arxiv-2512-06440.description: Abstract Neural Network Pruning has been established as driving force in the exploration of memory and energy efficient solutions with high throughput both during training and at test time. In this paper, we introduce a novel criterion for model compression, named “Expressiveness".

pmc-11612231.title: Probabilistic regression for autonomous terrain relative navigation via multi-modal feature learning
pmc-11612231.creator: Ickbum Kim, Sandeep Singh
pmc-11612231.description: The extension of human spaceflight across an ever-expanding domain, in conjunction with intricate mission architectures demands a paradigm shift in autonomous navigation algorithms, especially for the powered descent phase of planetary landing. Deep learning architectures have previously been explored to perform low-dimensional localization with limited success.

pmc-12384056.title: Development of a Novel Aptamer-Antibody Sandwich Chemiluminescent Biosensor and Its Application in the Detection of Aflatoxin B1
pmc-12384056.creator: Zhike Zhao, Jianghao Feng, Caizhang Wu
pmc-12384056.description: In addressing the challenges posed by high costs, low accuracy, and cumbersome operations in mycotoxin detection, a novel aptamer-antibody sandwich chemiluminescent biosensor for detecting aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) was developed. The indirect competition between AFB1, aflatoxin B1-ovomucoid complete antigen (AFB1-OVA), and rabbit anti-ovomucoid (OVA) antibody results in the formation of a sandwich complex.

pmc-12691127.title: Nasolacrimal Canal Topography in Relation to the Maxillary Position: CBCT Insights into Le Fort Osteotomy and Fixation Safety
pmc-12691127.creator: Mehmet Emre Yurttutan, Merve Berika Kadıoğlu, Mahzun Yıldız, Ömer Faruk Kocamaz, Meyra Durmaz, Mehmet Alp Eriş, Anıl Kamal, Dimitris Tatsis
pmc-12691127.description: Background/Objectives: Le Fort I osteotomy is a widely performed surgical procedure for correcting maxillary deformities, but it carries the risk of rare complications, including nasolacrimal duct (NLD) injury. This study evaluated the anatomical relationship between the nasolacrimal canal (NLC) and the maxilla across different skeletal patterns via cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) to define safer zones for fixation during orthognathic surgery.

pmc-12699556.title: Association of drinking water salinity with elevated blood pressure and risk of hypertension among coastal and other populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies
pmc-12699556.creator: Rajat Das Gupta, Setor K Kunutsor, David Eliecer Lopez-Salamanca, Fariha Tahsin Mercy, Nafisa Nawal, Carlos Espinal Tejada, Kunihiro Matsushita, Silvana Luciani, Anselm Hennis, Rajiv Chowdhury
pmc-12699556.description: BackgroundThe link between drinking water salinity and increased blood pressure and hypertension risk among coastal and other populations remains unclear. To investigate this, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies on drinking water salinity and cardiovascular outcomes.MethodsWe systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science for relevant studies published until 10 May 2025.

pmc-13172380.title: Conducting an RCT of a sexual health intervention during the COVID-19 pandemic: Lessons learned
pmc-13172380.creator: Cynthia Ann Graham, Nicole Stone, Stephen Bremner, Nuala McGrath, Rowena Bedford, Katherine Brown, Katie Newby, Amanda Clarke, Louise Jackson, Leanne Morrison, Tom Nadarzynski, Ye To
pmc-13172380.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). nsey Institute Home-Based Intervention Strategy (Kl-HIS) 1 to promote condom use among young men aged 16-25 years in England. We developed and feasibility tested two intervention delivery models: face-to-face (ProHIS 2 ) and digital-only (eHIS 3 ).

pmc-13226436.title: The Impact of Scaffolding on Academic Achievement in Undergraduate Emergency Language Courses
pmc-13226436.creator: An Zhu, Jian-Hong Ye
pmc-13226436.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The COVID-19 epidemic as a global public health emergency has brought unprecedented attention to emergency languages. Emergency language proficiency is an essential component of national language proficiency, making the development of emergency language service personnel particularly important. Therefore, in this study, 225 students of teaching Chinese to speakers of other languages at a Chinese university were invited to participate in a 8-week quasi-experimental design of a control group (traditional teaching) and an experimental group (scaffolded instruction) to conduct an emergency language course.

pmc-13367641.title: Rethinking Pain Assessment: Subjective Scales, Biomarkers, and Multimodal Integration
pmc-13367641.creator: Aifeng Liu, Longyao Zhang, Enyan Xue, Chao Zhang, Tianci Guo, Jida Wang, Dong Ming
pmc-13367641.description: Pain assessment is fundamental in pain medicine, anesthesiology, perioperative care, and clinical trials, yet it remains difficult to standardize across diseases, populations, and care settings. This review organizes pain assessment into four interrelated layers: subjective experience, behavioral and functional proxies, mechanistic biosignals, and multimodal integration.

pmc-13617366.title: Migraine care in the digital era: social listening insights and neurologists’ perspectives from Türkiye
pmc-13617366.creator: Derya Uluduz, Pınar Yalınay Dikmen, Burcin Yazici, Aynur Ozge
pmc-13617366.description: ObjectiveTo explore migraine-related concerns expressed in user-generated digital entries from a Turkish online health platform and contextualize them through neurologists’ expert perspectives. Background: Digital platforms may shape symptom interpretation, treatment expectations, and communication; however, social-listening findings require cautious interpretation given platform-related and methodological limitations.
